### (1) Hypotheses

Let

\[
\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3,\mu_4
\]

denote the true mean 8-week weight losses for the low-calorie, low-fat, low-carbohydrate, and control groups, respectively.

The one-way ANOVA hypotheses are

\[
H_0:\mu_1=\mu_2=\mu_3=\mu_4
\]

versus

\[
H_a:\text{not all four means are equal.}
\]

Equivalently, at least one diet group has a different mean weight loss.

---

### (2) ANOVA table

There are \(k=4\) groups with \(n_i=4\) subjects each, so

\[
N=16.
\]

Thus the degrees of freedom are:

\[
df_{\text{diet}}=k-1=3,
\]

\[
df_{\text{error}}=N-k=12,
\]

\[
df_{\text{total}}=N-1=15.
\]

You are given

\[
SS_{\text{total}}=114.4.
\]

Let

\[
SS_{\text{diet}}=4\sum_{i=1}^4(\bar y_{i\cdot}-\bar y_{\cdot\cdot})^2
\]

be the between-diet sum of squares. Then

\[
SS_{\text{error}}=114.4-SS_{\text{diet}}.
\]

So the ANOVA table is

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{Source} & df & SS & MS & F \\
\hline
\text{Diet} & 3 & SS_{\text{diet}} & SS_{\text{diet}}/3 
& \dfrac{SS_{\text{diet}}/3}{(114.4-SS_{\text{diet}})/12} \\
\text{Error} & 12 & 114.4-SS_{\text{diet}} 
& \dfrac{114.4-SS_{\text{diet}}}{12} & \\
\hline
\text{Total} & 15 & 114.4 & & 
\end{array}
\]

Equivalently,

\[
F=\frac{SS_{\text{diet}}/3}{SS_{\text{error}}/12}.
\]

---

### (3) Do we reject \(H_0\)?

As stated, the problem does **not** provide enough information to decide. We know the total sum of squares, but we also need either the raw data, the group means, \(SS_{\text{diet}}\), or \(SS_{\text{error}}\).

Assuming a standard \(\alpha=0.05\) test, the critical value is

\[
F_{0.95;3,12}\approx 3.49.
\]

We would reject \(H_0\) if

\[
F>3.49.
\]

Using the expression above,

\[
\frac{SS_{\text{diet}}/3}{(114.4-SS_{\text{diet}})/12}>3.49.
\]

This is equivalent to approximately

\[
SS_{\text{diet}}>53.3.
\]

So:

- If \(SS_{\text{diet}}>53.3\), reject \(H_0\).
- If \(SS_{\text{diet}}\le 53.3\), fail to reject \(H_0\).

But with only \(SS_{\text{total}}=114.4\), the rejection decision cannot be determined.
